d: Kuwait | IPO Readiness | Targeting Boursa Kuwait Premier Market | Full-time | On-site
A major Kuwait-headquartered regional group with substantial operations across the GCC is preparing for a planned IPO targeting Boursa Kuwait’s Premier Market.
This is an established, large-scale operating group entering its next stage of institutional development — not an early-stage business preparing to grow after listing.
We are looking for an experienced Director of Compliance to lead and strengthen the Group’s Governance and Compliance function through IPO readiness and into life as a listed company.

This is a senior, hands-on role with direct exposure to senior management and the Board. You will be the Group’s senior internal Governance and Compliance leader, with the mandate to strengthen the framework, close readiness gaps and develop the function for a listed-company environment.
q: You should have significant Governance and/or Compliance experience in Kuwait, with strong practical knowledge of CMA Kuwait, Boursa Kuwait and listed-company governance requirements.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have personally owned meaningful responsibilities involving regulatory interaction, disclosures, Governance or Compliance frameworks, Board reporting, inspections or remediation.

Direct experience within a Boursa Kuwait-listed company is strongly preferred but not mandatory. Candidates with substantial CMA/Boursa, IPO, governance-transformation or listed-company advisory experience will also be considered.
Experience supporting an IPO, listing or post-listing transition is a strong advantage.
Candidates from financial services are welcome where their experience extends beyond AML/CFT into broader corporate governance, disclosure and regulatory Compliance.
r: Lead the Governance and Compliance workstream for IPO readiness .
Assess existing arrangements, identify priority gaps and drive them through closure.
Lead implementation of applicable CMA Kuwait and Boursa Kuwait requirements .
Manage regulatory correspondence, submissions, inspections and remediation.
Strengthen policies, procedures, monitoring and reporting across Governance and Compliance.
Establish effective controls around disclosures, conflicts of interest, related-party transactions, insider matters, Code of Conduct and whistleblowing .
Provide clear Governance and Compliance reporting to senior management, the Board and Board Committees.
Work closely with Legal, Risk, Internal Control, Internal Audit, Finance and external IPO advisers.
Lead and develop the existing Compliance capability and build the team further as required.
Maintain a practical and proportionate approach to AML/KYC appropriate to the Group’s business.
x: This is an opportunity to take a senior leadership role in an already established regional group before listing, rather than join after the public-company framework has already been built.

You will help shape the Group’s Governance and Compliance architecture, work directly with senior management and the Board, develop the function and team, and continue leading it as part of the permanent listed-company structure.

d: Mott MacDonald is a global engineering, management and development consultancy committed to delivering impactful work that shapes the future. We are a team of over 20,000 experts working across more than 50 countries. As an employee-owned business, we invest in creating an environment where everyone feels valued, supported and empowered to do their best work.

Whether you want to deepen your expertise or broaden your experience across different projects and disciplines, you’ll be connected to a global community of specialists and have opportunities to shape your career.
We are looking for a Principal Public Health Engineer to join our Buildings team in the Middle East.

You will take a leading role in the design and delivery of public health engineering solutions across multidisciplinary building and infrastructure projects. Working closely with clients, architects and engineering teams, you will provide technical leadership from early design through detailed design and construction support.
This is an opportunity to combine hands-on engineering expertise with technical assurance, client engagement and the development of engineers within the team.
r: As Principal Public Health Engineer, your responsibilities will include:
Lead the design and technical delivery of public health engineering systems across multidisciplinary projects.
Develop and review designs for fire protection systems including sprinkler, standpipes, foam, clean agent and specialised fire protection systems.
Develop and review designs for natural gas and LPG systems associated with buildings.
Undertake and review engineering calculations, system sizing, equipment selection, technical drawings, specifications, technical reports and design documentation.
Support engineering team in design, design coordination and modelling.
Shall be experienced in local authority regulations and design approvals.
Shall be experienced in using national and international codes and standards associated with the public health engineering.
Provide technical assurance and undertake design reviews to ensure outputs meet project requirements and relevant standards.
Lead the public health engineering input from concept and feasibility through detailed, tender and IFC designs, with construction support as required.
Coordinate public health systems with key disciplines including mechanical, electrical, structural, landscape, pool, interior design and architectural disciplines.
Identify design constraints, interfaces, risks and opportunities and develop practical engineering solutions.
Work closely with clients and project stakeholders, providing clear technical advice and representing the discipline at project and design meetings.
Support project managers with scope, programme, resource planning and delivery.
Review technical submissions and respond to technical queries during project delivery.
Provide guidance, mentoring and technical support to engineers and other members of the team.
Contribute to proposals, bids and technical inputs for new opportunities where required.
Support continuous improvement and digital ways of working, sharing technical knowledge and lessons learned.
Demonstrate safe, ethical and inclusive behaviours aligned with Mott MacDonald values.
We are looking for someone who can bring strong public health engineering capability together with the judgement and collaborative approach expected at Principal level.
Degree in mechanical engineering, building services engineering or a relevant engineering discipline.
Minimum experience of 12 years, local experience would be preferable.
Strong professional experience in public health engineering and building services design.
Demonstrable experience designing water supply, drainage and associated public health systems.
Demonstrable experience designing gas and fire protection systems.
Experience delivering designs through multiple stages of the project lifecycle.
Strong understanding of engineering calculations, specifications, drawings and technical documentation.
Ability to review engineering designs and provide effective technical assurance.
Experience working within multidisciplinary design teams.
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical matters clearly to clients, colleagues and project stakeholders.
Ability to organise and prioritise work across multiple project requirements.
Ability to guide and develop less experienced engineers.
Chartered Engineer status, or progress towards an appropriate professional qualification.
Experience delivering major buildings or infrastructure programmes in the Middle East.
Experience across sectors such as healthcare, commercial, hospitality, residential, education, aviation, transport or major mixed-use developments.
Knowledge of regional authority requirements alongside relevant international standards and codes.
Experience of BIM-led and digitally integrated multidisciplinary design.
Experience supporting bids, proposals and client development activities.
Our benefits vary by country and are subject to eligibility and local policy. We’ll confirm the details relevant to you as part of the offer process.
Annual leave in line with local policy (competitive within the market).
Maternity leave above and beyond local provisions and paternity leave provisions where applicable
Medical insurance and life insurance as per local plan (standard and enhanced coverage may vary by country and policy).
Learning and career development through project variety, technical networks, and structured development opportunities.
An inclusive culture: we’re committed to equality, diversity and inclusion, and creating a workplace where everyone feels valued and supported.

Rewards and bonuses: we are owned by our people (no external investors) and through our employee ownership model success is shared through annual bonus opportunities and longer-term participation as your career grows (subject to local plan, eligibility and business performance)

d: The Purchasing Officer supports the Supply Chain Supervisor in sourcing and purchasing for the Bahrain generator factory and the wider business. The role turns approved purchase requests into purchase orders and follows each order through to delivery, supplier payment and PO closure in the ERP system. It also supports sourcing and supplier onboarding as GJG moves from a small number of overseas sources to local suppliers and direct buying from component manufacturers.
q: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field.
2–4 years of experience in purchasing, preferably in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Hands-on purchasing experience in an ERP system.
Working knowledge of Incoterms, the RFQ and quotation comparison process, and basic negotiation.
Fluent in English and Arabic, spoken and written, to work with local and international suppliers.
Experience sourcing from local GCC suppliers and international manufacturers.
Ability to read bills of materials and basic technical drawings for mechanical and electrical components.
CIPS or an equivalent purchasing certification, or working toward one.
r: Receive purchase requests from Production, Service, Engineering and other departments, and check that they are complete and approved before processing.
Create purchase orders in the ERP system, including raw material POs for production, and route them for approval in line with the Schedule of Authority.
Send approved purchase orders to suppliers and obtain order confirmation of price, quantity, delivery date and terms.
Follow up with suppliers and internal stakeholders until the material or service is delivered, and coordinate inbound shipments with Logistics.
Resolve delivery issues such as shortages, partial deliveries, damage, and price or quantity differences with the supplier and the receiving team.
Follow up with Finance on supplier invoices and payments so suppliers are paid on time, and close completed purchase orders in the ERP system.
Sourcing Support (as assigned by the Supply Chain Supervisor)
Prepare requests for quotation, collect and compare quotations, and recommend suppliers for raw material, components, services, tools and facility needs.
Support the development of local suppliers and purchasing from component manufacturers (engines, alternators, controllers and others), including NDAs, supplier documents and follow-up.
Track supplier prices, lead times and delivery performance, and keep supplier and price records up to date.
Final selection of direct material suppliers follows the supplier selection procedure (PRC-00780) and the Schedule of Authority.
Onboard new suppliers: collect the required documents, including acceptance of the Supplier Code of Conduct, NDA where needed, company and bank documents.
Create supplier accounts in the ERP system only after approval in line with the Schedule of Authority and a cleared Amber Road screening.
Maintain supplier master data. Any change to supplier bank details is verified with Finance before use.
Prepare and follow up on supplier credit application forms.
Maintain complete purchase order files and purchasing records, in line with document control and ISO 9001 requirements.
Prepare monthly purchasing reports, including open purchase orders, overdue deliveries and overdue supplier payments.
Comply with the Schedule of Authority, the Supplier Code of Conduct and Sustainable Procurement Policy, and company purchasing procedures, and declare any conflict of interest.
Collaborate with Production, Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Finance and Sales to support business objectives.
Cover customer order processing during the leave of the Sales Department order coordinator, as agreed between the Supply Chain and Sales Departments.

d: Are you an experienced Project Manager with a strong track record of delivering complex IT and digital transformation projects?

We are looking for a Sr. Project Manager to lead end-to-end project delivery, ensuring projects are completed within the agreed scope, schedule, budget, and quality standards while adhering to the Company's project governance framework.
q: Bachelor's degree or Diploma in Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
Minimum of 12 years of relevant experience in project management, particularly in IT and digital project delivery.
Proven experience delivering ERP, IT infrastructure, or Operational Technology (OT) projects.
Strong knowledge of project planning, budgeting, resource management, and contract management.
Proficiency in Microsoft Project and project management tools.
Experience in the Oil & Gas (O&G) industry is preferred.
Excellent leadership, stakeholder management, communication, and decision-making skills.
r: Lead and manage projects from initiation through planning, execution, monitoring, and closure.
Develop and manage project plans, schedules, budgets, resource allocations, and risk management strategies.
Coordinate internal teams, vendors, contractors, and other stakeholders to ensure successful project delivery.
Monitor project progress, manage dependencies, and implement corrective actions to address deviations.
Prepare and present project status reports to steering committees and senior management.
Apply the Company's project governance framework, stage-gate processes, and reporting requirements.
Manage change control, project risks, issues, and escalations throughout the project lifecycle.
Ensure proper project documentation, handover, and closure in accordance with established standards.
